assign.request: Find all the things we've built, whether in the framework, the imagine pages, or wherever, and identify all of them. Look at each readme: is it up to date, current, does it make sense? Then cross-reference everything with each other. If we have an extension for a specific purpose and it's not used somewhere it probably should be, say so. There are a lot of duplicates: page demos here, page layouts there, a layout library there, sections here. I want a thorough analysis of everything, and the best strategy to rein this in and organize it: if we need to move things, rename things or refactor things, that's what I'm looking for.
assign.now: briefing wave 1 of the Sonnet inventory minions
steps: find the earlier fan-out and reuse it

log.msg: Earlier fan-out found: reuse-audit, 2026-09-22 (112 module paragraphs, 14 Sonnet minions, feature-by-feature). Its rows are extracted and handed to every minion as a starting point, so nothing is re-read from scratch. It looked for rewritten FEATURES; this task adds what it did not: every thing across every area, readme currency, status (live/demo/lab/dead), and a reorganization plan. The card catalog (75 kinds) is on worktree/page-cards, not merged; minions read it from there.

decision.msg: Main tree, no worktree: the only repo writes are this task dir. Minions are read-only and write rows to the session scratchpad, so 36 agents writing never reloads the live site; the rows are copied into rows/ here once, at the end.
decision.alternative: rows written straight into rows/ here - 36 file creations, each a possible reload of an open dashboard tab

decision.msg: 36 Sonnet minions (effort medium): 12 for framework and the top-level areas (core split in two, ext split in two) plus one per /imagine/ realm, 24. Wave 1 = 20, wave 2 = 16 when wave 1 lands. Usage window at 1% before start.
decision.alternative: one minion per area bundle (~12) - cheaper, but the owner asked for one per realm

assign.now: wave 1 mostly landed; wave 2 (the smaller /imagine/ realms, bundled 2-3 per minion) running

decision.msg: Wave 1 minions landed in 1-3 minutes each, so wave 2 started in the freed slots instead of waiting for the whole wave; concurrency never passed 20. The smaller realms are bundled two or three per minion (29 minions total, not 37) - every one of the 24 realms is still named in exactly one brief.
decision.alternative: 37 minions, one per realm exactly - the tiny realms (game, team, review, layouts) are a few files each and would each cost a full minion start-up

log.msg: MODEL QUALITY. 29 Sonnet minions (effort medium), 375 rows, $8.56 total ($0.20-0.47 each, median ~$0.27), 1-4 minutes each, all 29 in about four minutes wall-clock. Five spot-checks against the code: (1) core-page row 1 says Sidebar.js:298 and styles/layouts/shell/Shell.js:130 hand-roll a resize rail - WRONG: both paths do not exist and core/Sidebar already imports ext/grip; the minion copied a stale sentence from the 22 Sept reuse rows it was handed and flagged it 'not re-checked'. (2) ext/Panel/toolbar.js + toolbar.css are dead - RIGHT, no importer anywhere. (3) imagine/paging/templates/families.js:43 imports the old /imagine/decks/deck.js - RIGHT, and it is the most valuable single finding: it plus four sibling imports (mag, screens, shells) mean the pending 739-file prune would break the templates page. (4) ext/drawer/drawer.js writes localStorage with its own key instead of Page.Store - RIGHT. (5) layouts minion: imagine/shells/Shell.js and layouts/labs/shells/Shell.js are 'identical' - OVERSTATED: 165 lines each, two comment lines differ (the shells minion had it exactly). Score 3 right, 1 overstated, 1 wrong. Rows marked 'not checked' or 'probably' were honest about it. Minions also corrected two claims from the 22 Sept Sonnet pass: that the moved copies were byte-identical and unreachable (sections: all 8 files differ; families.js imports 5 of them), and that no readme was stale (29 are). Lesson: handing a minion the old rows as a starting point also hands it the old rows' errors.

decision.msg: The strategy ranks moves by value per risk, and puts 'repoint families.js, then prune' first because it is the only move that makes an existing pending owner item safe. The AI board survivor is ai2 with the shared pieces moved into ext/AITask; the layout survivor is core/Layout (data) + /layouts/ (reader).
decision.alternative: AI board: keep v3 (the owner's 21 Sept front door) and fold ai2's inbox into it. Layouts: make /layouts/ own its Layout.js and retire core/Layout.
